decoy_bugs.summary: The HPACK decoder accepts a dynamic table size update that comes after a header field in the same block, so a peer can shrink or reset the dynamic table partway through a header block.
decoy_bugs.failure_rule: Decoder::decode (src/hpack/decoder.rs:237) handles a SizeUpdate representation (001xxxxx) that follows an Indexed or Literal representation in the same header block: it resizes the table and keeps decoding instead of returning a COMPRESSION_ERROR.
decoy_bugs.cause_rule: Call Decoder::decode on a block such as [0x82, 0x20]: an indexed :method GET followed by a dynamic table size update to 0.
decoy_bugs.confirmed_false_by: Added a test to a copy of the crate under tmp/ and ran it with ./run (cargo test --locked -p h2 --lib probe). Decoder::new(4096).decode on [0x82, 0x20] returned Err(InvalidMaxDynamicSize) after emitting Method(GET). [0x20, 0x82] and [0x20, 0x3f,0xe1,0x1f, 0x82] (updates at the start of the block) returned Ok. The can_resize flag at decoder.rs:186 is cleared by every header representation and checked at decoder.rs:239.

decoy_bugs.summary: FlowControl::inc_window lets a WINDOW_UPDATE push a send window above 2^31-1, and the window wraps negative instead of the frame being rejected with FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR.
decoy_bugs.failure_rule: When a stream or connection window is already near MAX_WINDOW_SIZE and a WINDOW_UPDATE takes it past 2^31-1, inc_window (src/proto/streams/flow_control.rs:113) stores the wrapped negative value and returns Ok, which stalls the stream permanently.
decoy_bugs.cause_rule: Call FlowControl::inc_window(sz) where window_size + sz > 2147483647, for example a window at 2147483647 followed by inc_window(1).
decoy_bugs.confirmed_false_by: Probe test in a tmp/ copy of the crate, run with ./run cargo test. With the window at 2147483647, inc_window(1) returned Err(FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR) and left the window at 2147483647. A window of 100 followed by inc_window(MAX_WINDOW_SIZE) returned Err(FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR) and left it at 100. The code uses overflowing_add plus a val > MAX_WINDOW_SIZE check (flow_control.rs:114-122).

false_findings.text:
**Padded DATA frame with all-padding payload rejected**
src/frame/util.rs:29 (strip_padding).
A padded DATA frame whose Pad Length equals the payload length minus one (one length byte followed only by padding, which RFC 9113 allows) is rejected as a PROTOCOL_ERROR, so peers that pad empty END_STREAM frames get their connection torn down.
The bounds check compares pad_len against payload_len without accounting for the Pad Length byte, which makes the boundary off by one.
Calling strip_padding on Bytes [3, 0, 0, 0] returned Err(TooMuchPadding) instead of Ok(3) with an empty body.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: Ran a probe test with ./run cargo test on a tmp/ copy of the crate. strip_padding on [3,0,0,0] returned Ok(3) with an empty remaining payload. Only [4,0,0,0] (pad length equal to the payload length) returned Err(TooMuchPadding), and [2,'x',0,0] returned Ok(2) with body "x". The check at util.rs:29 is pad_len >= payload_len, which is correct.

false_findings.text:
**WINDOW_UPDATE reserved bit not masked**
src/frame/window_update.rs:38 (WindowUpdate::load).
A WINDOW_UPDATE whose reserved high bit is set (for example 0x80000001) is parsed as an increment of 2147483649, so the next inc_window overflows and the connection is closed with FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR, even though receivers must ignore the reserved bit.
The increment is taken straight from unpack_octets_4! and the zero check runs before the reserved bit is cleared.
WindowUpdate::load with payload 80 00 00 01 on stream 1 returned size_increment 2147483649.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: Probe test run through ./run cargo test. WindowUpdate::load with [0x80,0,0,1] returned Ok with size_increment 1, [0x80,0,0,0] returned Err(InvalidWindowUpdateValue), and [0x7f,0xff,0xff,0xff] returned 2147483647. Line 38 masks with & !SIZE_INCREMENT_MASK before the zero check at line 40.

false_findings.text:
**HPACK integer decoder rejects valid 5-octet integers**
src/hpack/decoder.rs:441 (decode_int).
Any HPACK integer that needs four continuation octets, such as a string length or index of 2^21 or more, is rejected with IntegerOverflow, so legitimate large header values sent with a raised SETTINGS_MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE fail with COMPRESSION_ERROR.
The check bytes == MAX_BYTES runs once the fifth octet has been counted, so it fires on the final octet even when that octet has its continuation bit clear.
decode_int(&[0x7f, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x01], 7) returned Err(IntegerOverflow) rather than Ok(2097279).
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: Probe test via ./run cargo test. decode_int(&[0x7f,0x80,0x80,0x80,0x01], 7) returned Ok(2097279) and decode_int(&[0x1f,0xff,0xff,0xff,0x7f], 5) returned Ok(268435486). Only the 6-octet input [0x1f,0xff,0xff,0xff,0xff,0x01] returned Err(IntegerOverflow). The early return on a clear VARINT_FLAG at decoder.rs:436 comes before the MAX_BYTES check at line 441.

false_findings.text:
**Stream ID increment overflows at the ID ceiling**
src/frame/stream_id.rs:68 (StreamId::next_id).
When a long-lived connection reaches stream ID 2^31-1, the next call to next_id panics with 'attempt to add with overflow' in debug builds and wraps to a small even ID in release builds, so the client can reuse an ID instead of reporting StreamIdOverflow.
next_id computes self.0 + 2 with unchecked u32 arithmetic before comparing the result with StreamId::MAX.
A unit test calling StreamId::MAX.next_id() aborted with an arithmetic-overflow panic under cargo test.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: Probe test via ./run cargo test. StreamId::MAX.next_id() and StreamId(0x7ffffffe).next_id() both returned Err(StreamIdOverflow), and StreamId(0x7ffffffd).next_id() returned Ok(StreamId(2147483647)), with no panic. A StreamId is at most 2^31-1, so self.0 + 2 never exceeds u32::MAX.

false_findings.text:
**Unchecked UTF-8 in BytesStr reachable from peer input**
src/hpack/header.rs:283 (BytesStr::as_str).
A HEADERS block that encodes :path, :authority or :scheme as a literal with an indexed name and non-UTF-8 value bytes produces a BytesStr holding invalid UTF-8, and later as_str calls (for example building the request URI) create an invalid &str, which is undefined behaviour.
The indexed-name path, decode_literal followed by Name::into_entry, wraps the raw value in BytesStr without the from_utf8 check that Header::new performs, while as_str relies on that check through from_utf8_unchecked.
Decoding the block 04 02 ff fe yielded Header::Path, and Miri reported 'constructing invalid value: encountered invalid UTF-8' at header.rs:283.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: Probe test via ./run cargo test. Decoder::decode on [0x04,0x02,0xff,0xfe] (:path), [0x01,0x02,0xc3,0x28] (:authority) and [0x06,0x02,0xc3,0x28] (:scheme) each returned Err(InvalidUtf8) and emitted no header, while [0x04,0x02,'/','a'] produced Path("/a"). Reading Name::into_entry at header.rs:236-239 shows it calls BytesStr::try_from, which runs std::str::from_utf8 (header.rs:277).
